question: to the Commission Carmen Crespo Díaz (PPE), Isabelle Le Callennec (PPE), Paulo do Nascimento Cabral (PPE), Fredis Beleris (PPE), Niclas Herbst (PPE), Marco Falcone (PPE), Željana Zovko (PPE), Jessica Polfjärd (PPE), Susana Solís Pérez (PPE), Magdalena Adamowicz (PPE), Bartosz Arłukowicz (PPE), Francisco José Millán Mon (PPE), Javier Zarzalejos (PPE), Willemien Koning (PPE) Subject:

On 16 June 2026, during the plenary debate in Strasbourg on simplification and competitiveness, European Commissioner for Economy and Productivity; Implementation and Simplification Valdis Dombrovskis announced that the Commission is working on a ‘simplification package’ for the fisheries sector. The European fisheries and aquaculture sectors have repeatedly called for a reduction in administrative burdens and a simplification of the regulatory framework. The recent evaluation of the common fisheries policy also identified opportunities to simplify existing legislation and improve its implementation. Given the urgency of these concerns and the need to provide legal certainty and boost the competitiveness of the fisheries sector, we ask the Commission: 1.
What is the indicative timetable for presenting the forthcoming fisheries simplification package?

It is important to clarify whether the Commission envisages reviewing the common fisheries policy (including the landing obligation), the Fisheries Control Regulation1, the Common Market Organisation Regulation2, the multiannual management plans, the Deep-Sea Access Regulation3, and the framework for the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund. Which legislative instruments does it intend to include in this package?

Given the importance of these reforms for the sector’s viability, what timeline does the Commission contemplate for the subsequent legislative process with the European Parliament and the Council, and how will it ensure that the package is adopted before the end of the current term?

The European fisheries and aquaculture sectors have repeatedly called for a reduction in administrative burdens and a simplification of the regulatory framework. The recent evaluation of the common fisheries policy also identified opportunities to simplify existing legislation and improve its implementation. Given the urgency of these concerns and the need to provide legal certainty and boost the competitiveness of the fisheries sector, we ask the Commission: 1.
What is the indicative timetable for presenting the forthcoming fisheries simplification package?

It is important to clarify whether the Commission envisages reviewing the common fisheries policy (including the landing obligation), the Fisheries Control Regulation (1), the common market Organisation Regulation (2), the multiannual management plans, the Deep-Sea Access Regulation (3), and the framework for the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund. Which legislative instruments does it intend to include in this package?

Given the importance of these reforms for the sector’s viability, what timeline does the Commission contemplate for the subsequent legislative process with the European Parliament and the Council, and how will it ensure that the package is adopted before the end of the current term?

(20 August 2026) The Commission is working on simplifying and reducing administrative burden in the area of fisheries and aquaculture. The recent evaluation (4) of the Common Fisheries Policy (CFP) regulation concluded that the instrument is fit for purpose while also identifying some areas for improvement. The Commission is preparing the possible next steps, which will include stakeholder consultations and an impact assessment before any proposal is tabled to introduce targeted changes. The Commission continues to examine existing legislation, for instance Regulation (EU) No 1379/2013 on the common organisation of the markets and will act on findings where appropriate. Work is more advanced specifically for the European Maritime Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund (EMFAF) Regulatio n (5) and the multiannual management plans (6).

Regulation (EU) 2023/2842 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 November 2023 amending Council Regulation (EC) No 1224/2009, and amending Council Regulations (EC) No 1967/2006 and (EC) No 1005/2008 and Regulations (EU) 2016/1139, (EU) 2017/2403 and (EU) 2019/473 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards fisheries control (OJ L, 2023/2842, 20.12.2023, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/2842/oj). Regulation (EU) No 1308/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 December 2013 establishing a common organisation of the markets in agricultural products and repealing Council Regulations (EEC) No 922/72, (EEC) No 234/79, (EC) No 1037/2001 and (EC) No 1234/2007 (OJ L 347, 20.12.2013, p. 671, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2013/1308/oj). Regulation (EU) 2016/2336 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 December 2016 establishing specific conditions for fishing for deep-sea stocks in the north-east Atlantic and provisions for fishing in international waters of the north-east Atlantic and repealing Council Regulation (EC) No 2347/2002 (OJ L 354, 23.12.2016, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/2336/oj). https://ec.europa.eu/transparency/documents-register/detail?ref=SWD(2026)120&lang=en. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2021/1139/oj/eng. For the Western Mediterranean multiannual plan, the initiative aims to foster a more balanced approach to mixed fisheries management, while ensuring that stocks are maintained at levels consistent with maximum sustainable yield. For the three Northern multiannual plans (Western Waters, North Sea and Baltic Sea), the aim is to enhance legal certainty and find a new balance supporting the long-term health and recovery of fisheries and fish stocks.

Public calls for evidence on these regulations have concluded (7), and the Commission expects to deliver proposals for targeted amendments in the autumn 2026. The Commission’s proposals will be limited in scope, to transpose the WTO agreement into the EMFAF Regulation and to simplify and provide flexibility in certain conditions, as well as clarifying certain provisions in the multiannual plans. The Commission understands the importance and value that such targeted amendments can bring to stakeholders, in accessing finance, fishing opportunities, and ensuring viable business models. Member States should also benefit from reduced burden and delays. Once these proposals are tabled, the Commission will therefore do its utmost to facilitate their swift adoption by the European Parliament and the Council, so that these targeted improvements enter into force as quicky as possible.
